liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): Reviewer believes this is the only time the band tried returning to Crazy Fingers after leaving it; Jerry sings nearly every lyric and plays beautiful leads; the transition into Miracle was creative [31][32]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer recalls a comic about a fan at these rain-soaked shows, saying an Other One in the rain was legendary; On the 27th, Phil ramped up perfectly into the first crescendo, and the band shredded the tune and stitched it back together [23][26]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-07-29.172806.senn441.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1982-07-29.167229.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 151 min [3]
- **gd1982-07-29.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102569.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the Wise recording's sound in-your-face and on par with other great 1982 shows [31]
- **gd1982-07-29.156430.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: source not stated; 21 songs; 153 min [10]. Said about its sound: No patch exists for the Drums > Space transition, so small fades were added at the track break [10]
- **gd82-07-29.fob-senn421.wise.4981.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 4.75/5 by 16 [16]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this Jim Wise audience recording incredibly good; Jerry's guitar only comes in about halfway through the opening Minglewood; Recording puts you among the crowd, with audible song callouts, but too much chatting and whooping; Recording is imperfect: Bob's rhythm guitar is overwhelmingly loud in the mix, burying Jerry [24][25][28]

## Around the show

- Unusual extended rain for Colorado at this time of year arrived and left with the band, falling across all three shows [27]
- Reviewer recalls word among heads that without a ticket you wouldn't get into the Rocks, though everyone seemed to get in [31]
- Reviewer neglected the Red Rocks shows because only audience tapes exist, while August 1982 has excellent soundboards [24]
- Reviewer thinks this show is better overall than the 27th, though the 27th's second set had the best Other One they'd heard [26]
- Reviewer sees the night as high-energy 1982 with musical experimentation and several rarities [28]
- Reviewer says it was the second Other One in three nights and suggests comparing it with 7/27/82 [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-07-29.172806.senn441.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Anon; transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M (TDK-MA-C90) [1]. Also: Master cassette recording and transfer came from anonymous benefactors; a Wise/Miller Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 0:43 patch in Drums > Space [1]
- **gd1982-07-29.167229.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Wiseman and Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [3]
- **gd1982-07-29.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102569.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [9]
- **gd1982-07-29.156430.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: taped by Concert recording by Rip Tompkins, & with thanks to Richie Stankiewicz!; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 04/2022; source: BeyerDynamic mics > Sony TC-D5M > TDK MA-90s [10]. Also: Possible match to another ID is uncertain; a different patch covers the first 14 seconds of Cold Rain & Snow [10]
- **gd82-07-29.fob-senn421.wise.4981.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [16]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1982-07-28 Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Morrison, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-07-28-red-rocks-amphitheatre-morrison-co-usa/) [34]

claims.text: Reviewer recalls a comic about a fan at these rain-soaked shows, saying an Other One in the rain was legendary
Reviewer calls this Jim Wise audience recording incredibly good; Jerry's guitar only comes in about halfway through the opening Minglewood
Reviewer neglected the Red Rocks shows because only audience tapes exist, while August 1982 has excellent soundboards
Recording puts you among the crowd, with audible song callouts, but too much chatting and whooping
Reviewer thinks this show is better overall than the 27th, though the 27th's second set had the best Other One they'd heard
On the 27th, Phil ramped up perfectly into the first crescendo, and the band shredded the tune and stitched it back together
Unusual extended rain for Colorado at this time of year arrived and left with the band, falling across all three shows
Recording is imperfect: Bob's rhythm guitar is overwhelmingly loud in the mix, burying Jerry
Reviewer sees the night as high-energy 1982 with musical experimentation and several rarities
Reviewer says it was the second Other One in three nights and suggests comparing it with 7/27/82
Reviewer believes this is the only time the band tried returning to Crazy Fingers after leaving it
Reviewer finds the Wise recording's sound in-your-face and on par with other great 1982 shows
Reviewer recalls word among heads that without a ticket you wouldn't get into the Rocks, though everyone seemed to get in
Jerry sings nearly every lyric and plays beautiful leads; the transition into Miracle was creative
Master cassette recording and transfer came from anonymous benefactors; a Wise/Miller Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 0:43 patch in Drums > Space
Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman, coordinated by Charlie Miller; Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source patches Drums and Around & Around
Possible match to another ID is uncertain; a different patch covers the first 14 seconds of Cold Rain & Snow
No patch exists for the Drums > Space transition, so small fades were added at the track break
